key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics, electrostatic storage, and ferroelectric/in-memory computing can be co-designed to power reliable edge AI with far lower communication and energy overhead than centralized data-center inference.
engineering_relevance: The paper highlights a materials-to-systems path for autonomous edge nodes by matching indoor energy harvesting with low-power computation and storage needs.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaic requirements for distributed intelligence power budgets
Survey emerging materials for energy harvesting, storage, and neuromorphic/in-memory computing
Argue for (anti)ferroelectrics as a shared platform for energy storage and low-power computation
evidence_signal: This is a perspective article synthesizing literature and design requirements rather than presenting new experimental performance data in the abstract.
watch_item: The main implementation challenge is aligning real-world IPV output, storage capacity, and device-level compute efficiency under variable indoor lighting and system integration constraints.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
